correctness.rationale: For wheel rim size m>=7, injectivity of the selected-neighbor signatures characterizes rim resolvability; a selected hub never distinguishes rim vertices, and at least three rim landmarks are necessary and sufficient to resolve the hub once rim vertices are resolved. Empty-signature collisions are exactly multiple 000 centers, and nonempty-signature collisions exactly 00100, yielding the gap constraints. Long gaps form an independent set of C_k, and a marked-root double count yields the stated binomial sum. Maximum capacity is floor(5k/2)+1; deficit 0,1,2 coefficient extraction gives all five basis-count formulas. Original BFS-based exhaustive checks verified 130944 rim subsets, both hub choices, and all coefficients for m=7..16; exact arithmetic checked residue formulas through m=200. Finite computation is supporting evidence, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2021 wheel paper already characterizes feasible gap patterns and determines metric dimension, neither of which is claimed original. New content is the evaluated all-cardinality binomial-sum resolving-set polynomial, its (1+z) center factor, and the five explicit labeled metric-basis count formulas. The closest inspected primary text does not count wheel resolving subsets or metric bases. The 2023 algorithmic enumeration paper is at different generality, and the 2020 missing-spoke paper concerns another graph family. An indexed/source-limited search cannot exclude an unindexed equivalent counting paper; the priority claim retains this explicit risk.
residual_risks: The 2021 exact structural gap criterion may make parts of this enumerative theorem a natural derivation; the evaluated counting formulas themselves were not located in inspected primary text.
Indexed and accessible-source coverage does not rule out older or nonindexed resolving-set enumeration under another name.
The 2020 missing-spoke-wheel paper was inspected through publisher HTML/abstract, not its full text; its stated object is different.

value.rationale: The all-cardinality resolving-set polynomial and explicit number of metric bases for each residue class refine a previously known scalar metric dimension into a complete natural counting invariant. This quantifies the number of landmark designs, distinguishes sharply different multiplicities at equal minimum size, and interprets the enumerator through independent sets of a cyclic gap graph. No arbitrary slice or routine scalar restatement is central to the claim.
